content.title: RULES EVERY NEW PARENT NEEDS FOR THEIR OWN {{BODY}}
facts: **Hydrate before coffee** – drink a full glass of water before your first cup to counter the dehydration from broken sleep.
**Nap in 20-minute blocks** – anything longer pushes you into deep sleep and leaves you groggier when the baby wakes you.
**Eat protein first thing** – 2 eggs or a handful of nuts in the morning blunts the energy crash that comes from running on adrenaline.
**Step outside for 5 minutes** – morning light resets your body clock even if your sleep schedule is completely broken.
**Stretch your neck and shoulders 2x/day** – constant bending over a crib or car seat tightens this area fast.
**Set a 7pm caffeine cutoff** – even exhausted, late caffeine will wreck the little sleep window you do get.
**Keep a snack stash within reach** – almonds, dates, or oat bars prevent the blood sugar dips that fuel short tempers.
**Ask for a 30-minute solo break daily** – your nervous system needs this to reset, not just your to-do list.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.

caption:
New parents run on fumes, and a few small swaps make a real difference. Drinking water before coffee matters because overnight dehydration shrinks blood volume slightly, which makes your heart work harder and amplifies that wired-but-tired feeling caffeine alone won't fix. Protein in the morning works because it slows glucose absorption, keeping your blood sugar steadier through the first chaotic hours instead of spiking and crashing. And that 5-minute step outside isn't just fresh air — morning light exposure helps suppress melatonin at the right time, which keeps your circadian rhythm from drifting further out of sync when your sleep is already fragmented. Everyone's situation is different, so adjust what fits your days.
